archetypes.name: vendor-flag-reentry
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly reverses #2449, which deliberately removed Codex from this panel — auditing all residual 'Codex absent' assumptions in the review pipeline is a unique risk not covered by the static panel.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every reference to `codex_present_for_waterfall`, `CODEX_PRESENT`, and any comment or conditional that was written under the assumption that Codex is excluded from the `/review` panel. Verify the plan touches every site that relies on `codex_present_for_waterfall="false"` being stable — including `check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh`, `dispatch-panel.sh`, and any callers that read or gate on that variable. Check whether the original reason for #2449 is documented anywhere in the codebase (commit messages, comments) and whether re-enablement addresses it or introduces the same problem. Identify any downstream scripts or tests that hardcode expectations of Cursor-only reviewer output filenames (`cursor-specialist-*`) and would silently misbehave when Codex specialist outputs appear. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: availability-math
archetypes.rationale: The plan replaces a hardcoded INTENDED_SLOTS=6 with an availability-derived formula across dispatch-panel.sh, review-core.sh, and check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh — verifying the formula is correct in all four vendor-combination states is a correctness check the static panel will not do systematically.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify the availability-derived `INTENDED_SLOTS` formula (proposed as `4 * (cursor_available + codex_available)`, floored at 4) produces the correct denominator in all four vendor-availability states: both up (→8), cursor-only (→4), codex-only (→4), both down (→4). Check that the `>50%` failure threshold fires correctly at each denominator: both-up panel needs >4 failures to hard-stop; single-vendor panel needs >2; both-down needs >2. Trace how `review-core.sh` derives and passes `--intended-slots` to `check-reviewer-failure-threshold.sh` and confirm the derivation matches the dispatch step's emitted slot count rather than re-computing independently. Flag any off-by-one or integer-division boundary that could cause a healthy panel to hard-stop or a critically failed panel to pass through. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: log-exclude-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds new Codex specialist output filenames that must be excluded from committed run logs — a gap in larch-log.sh exclusion patterns would silently commit large raw reviewer transcripts, a risk not addressed by any static archetype.
archetypes.prompt_body: Cross-reference every new output filename pattern the plan introduces — `codex-specialist-${name}-output.txt` (static), `dyn-${name}-codex-output.txt` (dynamic Codex twin), and any sidecar files (`.json`, `.meta`, error outputs) — against the exclusion filter logic in `scripts/larch-log.sh`. Verify that the existing Cursor specialist exclusion patterns (`cursor-specialist-*`) are not inadvertently narrowed or broken by the additions. Check whether the plan's larch-log regression test update covers both static Codex outputs and the dynamic Codex-twin naming convention, and flag any gap where the harness only asserts Cursor exclusion. Look at `scripts/larch-log.md` to confirm the documented exclusion contract stays in sync with the script change. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
